No bony destruction on orthopantomogram
Well-demarcated, hypoechoic solid mass on ultrasonography
Well-bordered, slightly enhancing soft-tissue tumor on CT
key_facts: 25-year-old woman presented with a painless lump in the left cheek
Mass was first noted nine months earlier
No toothache, numbness, or systemic symptoms
No significant medical history
Left facial asymmetry without skin changes
Firm, mobile, non-tender mass approximately 4 cm in diameter
Bulge of the left buccal mucosa with a well-defined, firm, non-tender mass intraorally
No cervical lymphadenopathy
Healed post-extraction socket in the region of tooth 36 on orthopantomogram
Ultrasonography showed a discrete, well-demarcated, hypoechoic solid mass
Contrast-enhanced CT revealed a well-bordered, slightly enhancing soft-tissue tumor
Mass was supplied by branches of the left buccal artery
Fine-needle aspiration biopsy showed no signs of malignancy
Intraoral incisional biopsy demonstrated wide fibroblast proliferation

shortlist.why_kept: Most common benign salivary gland tumor, consistent with painless lump and imaging findings

shortlist.label: Fibromatosis
shortlist.why_kept: Intraoral incisional biopsy demonstrated wide fibroblast proliferation, suggesting fibromatosis

shortlist.label: Lipoma
shortlist.why_kept: Firm, mobile, non-tender mass, possible lipoma given location and characteristics

shortlist.label: Neurofibroma
shortlist.why_kept: Possible given deep tissue involvement and well-defined mass on imaging

shortlist.label: Desmoid tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Aggressive fibromatosis variant, possible given biopsy findings and clinical presentation

raw.rationale: The presence of a well-bordered, slightly enhancing soft-tissue tumor with a discrete, well-demarcated, hypoechoic solid mass on ultrasonography and contrast-enhanced CT, along with the intraoral incisional biopsy demonstrating wide fibroblast proliferation, is most consistent with a pleomorphic adenoma, a common benign salivary gland tumor.

rejected.label: Fibromatosis
rejected.why: Fibromatosis is a more aggressive and infiltrative condition, which does not match the well-bordered nature of the mass described

rejected.label: Lipoma
rejected.why: Lipoma would typically appear as a more echogenic mass on ultrasonography due to its fatty content, which is not described here

rejected.label: Neurofibroma
rejected.why: Neurofibroma would more likely present with neurological symptoms or be part of a larger syndrome, which is not indicated in the case

rejected.label: Desmoid tumor
rejected.why: Desmoid tumors are known for their aggressive local growth and potential for recurrence, which does not align with the benign appearance and behavior of the mass in this case

rejected.label: Malrotation with chronic volvulus

shortlist.label: Contrast-Induced Encephalopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Patient received nonionic iodinated contrast (Iopromide) during catheterization, which is a known risk factor for contrast-induced encephalopathy

raw.rationale: The development of seizure-like activity approximately 12 hours after cardiac catheterization with nonionic iodinated contrast (Iopromide) and the noncontrast head CT showing a diffuse increase in cortical density without other intracranial abnormalities suggest a direct relationship between the contrast administration and the neurological symptoms.

rejected.label: Hypoxic-Ischemic Encephalopathy
rejected.why: While the patient experienced cardiorespiratory arrest, the seizure-like activity and CT findings are more closely timed with the contrast administration than the arrest.

rejected.label: Cerebral Edema
rejected.why: The CT findings do show increased cortical density, but the clinical context and timing more strongly suggest a contrast-induced effect rather than generalized cerebral edema.

rejected.label: Seizure Disorder
rejected.why: The seizure-like activity appears to be an acute reaction rather than a manifestation of a chronic seizure disorder, given the temporal relationship with the contrast administration.

rejected.label: Post-Pump Syndrome
rejected.why: The patient did not undergo a full pump procedure due to hemodynamic instability, making post-pump syndrome less likely as the primary cause of the neurological symptoms.

s1.syndrome_frame: Acute coronary syndrome with recurrent ventricular arrhythmias and evolving left ventricular dysfunction
salient_findings: Canadian Cardiovascular Society Class III angina

Recurrent sustained polymorphic ventricular tachycardia and ventricular fibrillation
Akinesia of all apical segments with severely reduced LVEF of 35%
key_facts: 67-year-old man with hypertension
Dyslipidaemia
Stage 3 chronic kidney disease
Active smoking (35 pack-years)
Family history of ischaemic heart disease
Prior percutaneous coronary interventions (2008, 2017, 2022) for non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction
Exercise stress test induced angina at 50 W without ECG changes
ECG showed normal sinus rhythm, Q waves in lead III, and biphasic T waves in leads III and aVF

ECG showed ST-segment elevation in leads V1–V3 after worsening chest pain

Cyst measuring 16 × 24 cm on ultrasonography and 30 × 25.6 × 16.8 cm on computed tomography
key_facts: 23-year-old woman
2-year history of progressive abdominal distension
Early satiety
Urinary urgency
No pain, weight loss, or systemic symptoms
Normal menstrual cycles
Mother had a history of ovarian cysts
Abdomen distended with dull percussion notes
No tenderness or guarding on examination
Cyst had a fluid density of 20 Hounsfield units
No calcifications, soft-tissue components, or enhancing septations on computed tomography
Laboratory studies, including tumor markers, were within normal limits
ROMA score was 4.1 %
Serological testing for Echinococcus granulosus was negative

differentials: Cystic solitary fibrous tumor of the peritoneum
per_call: Cystic solitary fibrous tumor of the peritoneum

raw.rationale: The large midline intraperitoneal cyst with a fluid density of 20 Hounsfield units and no calcifications, soft-tissue components, or enhancing septations is consistent with a mesenteric cyst, which is a benign abdominal cyst that can cause abdominal distension and compress adjacent organs.

rejected.label: Peritoneal inclusion cyst
rejected.why: Peritoneal inclusion cysts are typically associated with a history of abdominal surgery or trauma, which is not mentioned in the vignette.

rejected.label: Ovarian cystadenoma
rejected.why: Ovarian cystadenoma would likely be more lateral in location and may have a more complex appearance on imaging, which is not consistent with the large midline cyst described.

rejected.label: Simple peritoneal cyst
rejected.why: Simple peritoneal cysts are typically smaller and may not cause significant abdominal distension or compression of adjacent organs.

rejected.label: Cystic mesothelioma
rejected.why: Cystic mesothelioma is a rare malignant tumor that would likely have a more complex appearance on imaging and may have elevated tumor markers, which is not consistent with the benign appearance and normal laboratory studies in this case.

s1.syndrome_frame: Subacute onset of cerebellar syndrome with increased intracranial pressure
salient_findings: Severe occipital and temporal headaches
Bilateral blurry vision and morning projectile vomiting
Kinetic and static cerebellar syndrome with ataxia, imbalance, uncoordinated movements, bilateral nystagmus, and stage I bilateral papilledema
Inferior median oval lesion of the cerebellar vermis on brain MRI
key_facts: 44-year-old woman
4-month history of severe headaches
Headaches are paroxysmal and aggravated by changes in position
Associated with bilateral blurry vision and morning projectile vomiting
Neurological examination shows cerebellar syndrome
Ataxia, imbalance, uncoordinated movements, bilateral nystagmus, and stage I bilateral papilledema are present
Routine blood tests are unremarkable
Noncontrast CT of the head shows no abnormalities
Brain MRI shows an inferior median oval lesion of the cerebellar vermis
Lesion measures 40 × 31 × 29 mm
Lesion is hypointense on T1-weighted images and heterogeneously hyperintense on T2-weighted images
Lesion shows heterogeneous enhancement after gadolinium administration
Lesion fills the foramen of Magendie and exerts mass effect on the medulla
No surrounding edema on FLAIR
Diffusion-weighted imaging demonstrates increased signal
GRE T2* sequences show no hemorrhage or calcification
Magnetic resonance spectroscopy shows an elevated choline peak and reduced N-acetyl aspartate signal

raw.rationale: The patient's age, symptoms, and imaging findings are consistent with medulloblastoma, a common malignant brain tumor in adults that often arises in the cerebellum and can cause increased intracranial pressure and cerebellar syndrome.

rejected.label: Pilocytic astrocytoma
rejected.why: Typically has a more benign course and imaging characteristics, such as a cystic component with an enhancing mural nodule, which is not described in this case

rejected.label: Ependymoma
rejected.why: Often arises from the ependymal lining of the ventricles or central canal and may have a more heterogeneous appearance on imaging, but the described location and imaging characteristics are not as typical for ependymoma

rejected.label: Hemangioblastoma
rejected.why: Usually has a distinct appearance on imaging with a cystic component and a strongly enhancing mural nodule, and is often associated with von Hippel-Lindau disease, which is not mentioned in the case

rejected.label: Cerebellar primitive neuroectodermal tumor
rejected.why: A rare and aggressive tumor that can have similar imaging characteristics to medulloblastoma, but the clinical presentation and imaging findings in this case are more consistent with medulloblastoma

s1.syndrome_frame: A middle-aged woman with a history of cancer presenting with a new onset of neurological symptoms and a mass lesion in the brain
salient_findings: History of breast cancer
New onset of persistent headache
Mass lesion in the right temporal lobe
key_facts: 46-year-old Japanese woman
History of epilepsy
History of breast cancer
Redness and swelling of the right breast
Erythema and swelling in the lower right breast
Ultrasound revealed a low-echo mass with partially unclear margins in the outer right breast
Biopsy showed invasive ductal carcinoma
High grade, ER+, PgR–, HER2 3+, Ki67 70%
Whole-body PET-CT revealed increased uptake in the right axilla, anterior mediastinum, left pleura, and liver
Received four cycles of FEC chemotherapy
Received trastuzumab plus pertuzumab with docetaxel
Achieved a clinical complete response maintained for 23 months
Developed a persistent headache two years after treatment initiation
CT and MRI of the head revealed a 30-mm mass lesion in the right temporal lobe
